p.src: Now Jia Xu, having discerned Cao Cao's intention, resolved to turn the stratagem against him. He said to Zhang Xiu, “From atop the walls, I have watched Cao Cao circle the city and inspect it for three days. He noticed that the bricks and earth at the southeastern corner differ in color, some new and some old, and that most of the defensive chevaux-de-frise are broken. He therefore means to attack and enter there. Yet he is making a show of piling grass in the northwest, hoping to deceive us into withdrawing our troops to defend that quarter. Under cover of darkness, he will surely scale the southeastern corner.” Zhang Xiu asked, “Then what are we to do?” Jia Xu replied, “That is easily managed. Tomorrow, have the strongest soldiers eat their fill, travel light, and conceal themselves in the houses of the southeast. Then dress the common people as soldiers and have them make a pretense of defending the northwest. At night, allow the enemy to scale the southeastern corner. Once they have climbed into the city, let a cannon sound; the ambushers will rise together, and Cao Cao can be captured.”

p.src: Zhang Xiu was delighted and followed his plan. Before long, a scout reported to Cao Cao that Zhang Xiu had withdrawn all his troops to the northwestern corner, where they shouted as they defended the city, while the southeast was exceedingly empty. Cao Cao said, “He has fallen into my trap!” He secretly ordered the army to prepare spades, mattocks, and scaling equipment, while by day he led his forces only against the northwestern corner. At the second watch, however, he led picked troops into the moat at the southeastern corner and had the chevaux-de-frise hacked apart. There was no movement at all within the city, and the soldiers surged in together. Suddenly a cannon sounded, and ambushing troops rose on every side. Cao Cao's troops hastened to retreat, but Zhang Xiu himself drove his valiant men against them from the rear. Cao Cao's army suffered a crushing defeat, withdrew beyond the city, and fled for several dozen li. Zhang Xiu pursued and slew them until dawn, only then recalling his troops into the city. When Cao Cao counted the remnants of his defeated army, he found that more than fifty thousand men had been lost, together with innumerable baggage and supplies. Lü Qian and Yu Jin had both been wounded.

p.src: Now when Jia Xu saw Cao Cao flee in defeat, he urgently advised Zhang Xiu to send Liu Biao a letter asking him to raise troops and cut off Cao Cao's line of retreat. On receiving the letter, Liu Biao was about to mobilize his army when a scout suddenly reported that Sun Ce had stationed troops at Hukou. Kuai Liang said, “Sun Ce's stationing troops at Hukou is part of Cao Cao's scheme. Cao Cao has just been defeated. If we do not seize the advantage and strike him now, he will surely become a threat later.” Liu Biao therefore ordered Huang Zu to hold the strategic passes firmly, while he himself led troops to Anzhong County to cut off Cao Cao's retreat. At the same time, he arranged to join forces with Zhang Xiu. Learning that Liu Biao's army had mobilized, Zhang Xiu and Jia Xu immediately led their troops in pursuit of Cao Cao.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Cao's army advanced slowly. On reaching the Yu River by Xiangcheng, Cao Cao suddenly burst into loud weeping on horseback. Everyone was startled and asked him why. Cao Cao said, “I was thinking of how I lost my great general Dian Wei here last year. I could not help but weep!” He therefore ordered the army to halt and made lavish preparations for a sacrificial feast to mourn the departed spirit of Dian Wei. Cao Cao personally offered incense, wept, and bowed; throughout the army, none remained unmoved. After sacrificing to Dian Wei, he offered sacrifices to his nephew Cao Anmin, his eldest son Cao Ang, and the soldiers who had fallen in battle. He even made an offering to the Dayuan horse that had been shot dead.

p.src: The next day, a messenger suddenly arrived from Xun Yu with this report: “Liu Biao is aiding Zhang Xiu and has stationed troops at Anzhong, cutting off our return route.” Cao Cao replied to Xun Yu in a letter: “I advance only a few li each day, not because I am unaware that the enemy is pursuing me, but because my plan is already settled. Once I reach Anzhong, I shall assuredly defeat Zhang Xiu. You need have no doubts.” He then hastened the army onward to the borders of Anzhong County. Liu Biao's army had already occupied the strategic ground, while Zhang Xiu came up behind with his troops. Under cover of night, Cao Cao ordered his soldiers to cut a road through the difficult terrain and secretly planted an ambush.

p.src: At first light, the armies of Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu joined together. Seeing that Cao Cao had few soldiers, they suspected he had fled and both led their forces into the defile to attack him. Cao Cao unleashed his hidden troops and utterly defeated both armies. Cao Cao's troops emerged from the Anzhong boundary pass and made camp beyond the defile. Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu each rallied their defeated troops and met together. Liu Biao said, “Who could have expected us to fall instead into Cao Cao's treacherous scheme!” Zhang Xiu said, “Let us devise another plan!” Thereupon the two armies assembled at Anzhong.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xun Yu learned that Yuan Shao intended to raise an army against the capital at Xu, and sent an urgent letter by night to Cao Cao. Cao Cao was alarmed on receiving the letter and turned his army homeward that very day. A spy reported this to Zhang Xiu, who wished to pursue. Jia Xu said, “You must not pursue them. If you do, you will surely be defeated.” Liu Biao said, “If we do not pursue today, we shall sit idle and lose our opportunity.” He strongly urged Zhang Xiu to lead more than ten thousand troops in pursuit with him. After traveling some ten li, they caught up with Cao Cao's rear guard. Cao Cao's troops fought with all their might, and the armies of Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao were routed and returned in defeat. Zhang Xiu said to Jia Xu, “I did not heed your words, and this defeat has indeed come to pass.” Jia Xu said, “Now you should reorganize the troops and pursue them once more.” Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao both said, “We have already been defeated. How can we pursue them again?” Jia Xu said, “If you pursue them this time, you will surely win a great victory. If it proves otherwise, I ask that you cut off my head.” Zhang Xiu believed him. Liu Biao remained doubtful and refused to accompany him. Zhang Xiu therefore led a force in pursuit by himself. Cao Cao's troops were indeed badly defeated, abandoning soldiers, horses, and baggage all along the road as they fled.

p.src: As Zhang Xiu pressed forward in pursuit, a strong body of troops suddenly surged out from behind a hill. Zhang Xiu dared pursue no farther and withdrew his army to Anzhong. Liu Biao asked Jia Xu, “Earlier, when picked troops pursued a retreating army, you said they would surely be defeated. Later, when defeated troops attacked a victorious army, you said they would surely prevail. In the end, everything happened exactly as you said. How could such different circumstances both confirm your prediction? I beg you to explain it clearly to me.” Jia Xu replied, “It is easy to understand. Though General Zhang is skilled in the use of troops, he is no match for Cao Cao. Although Cao Cao's army had been defeated, he was certain to leave a valiant commander to guard the rear against pursuit. Though our troops were keen for battle, they could not overcome such a force. That is how I knew they would surely be defeated. As for Cao Cao's urgent retreat, some crisis must have arisen in the capital at Xu. After defeating our pursuers, he would certainly hurry home with light carriages and make no further preparations against attack. By pursuing again and taking advantage of his unpreparedness, we were therefore able to win.” Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu both acknowledged the superiority of his insight. Jia Xu advised Liu Biao to return to Jingzhou and Zhang Xiu to defend Xiangcheng, so that they might support each other like lips and teeth. The two armies then dispersed.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Cao Cao was marching, he heard that his rear guard was being pursued by Zhang Xiu and hurriedly led his generals back to its aid. He found that Zhang Xiu's army had already withdrawn. The defeated soldiers returned and told him, “Had this force from behind the hills not blocked the central road, we would all have been captured.” Cao Cao hastily asked who the man was. The man lowered his spear, dismounted, and bowed before Cao Cao. He was a Commandant of the Household Who Quells Might, a native of Pingchun in Jiangxia. His surname was Li, his given name Tong, and his courtesy name Wenda. Cao Cao asked where he had come from. Li Tong replied, “I have lately been guarding Runan. Hearing that the Chancellor was at war with Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao, I came especially to provide support.” Cao Cao was delighted. He enfeoffed Li Tong as Marquis Who Establishes Merit and appointed him to guard the western border of Runan against Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu. Li Tong bowed his thanks and departed.

p.src: Guo Jia said, “You know that Liu Bang and Xiang Yu were no match for each other. Gaozu prevailed solely through wisdom; though Xiang Yu was strong, he was captured in the end. Now Yuan Shao has ten grounds for defeat, while you possess ten grounds for victory. Though Shao’s forces are numerous, they are not to be feared. Shao is burdened with elaborate rites and endless formalities; you act according to what is natural. This is your victory in principle. Shao acts in defiance of rightful order; you lead in accordance with it. This is your victory in righteousness. Since the reigns of Emperors Huan and Ling, government has suffered from excessive leniency. Shao compounds this with further leniency, while you correct it with severity. This is your victory in governance. Shao appears generous but is inwardly jealous, and most of those he employs are his own kin. You seem plain in manner but are discerning within, and employ men solely for their ability. This is your victory in breadth of mind. Shao makes many plans but few decisions; once you obtain a sound plan, you act at once. This is your victory in strategy. Shao is intent only on gathering fame; you treat men with perfect sincerity. This is your victory in virtue. Shao cares for those near him but neglects those afar; your concern extends everywhere. This is your victory in benevolence. Shao listens to slander and is led into confusion; insidious accusations find no purchase with you. This is your victory in discernment. Shao confounds right and wrong; your laws and standards are strict and clear. This is your victory in civil order. Shao delights in empty displays of force and does not understand the essentials of warfare; you overcome multitudes with a few and wield troops with divine skill. This is your victory in arms. With these ten grounds for victory, it will be no difficult matter for you to defeat Shao.”

p.src: Now Gao Shun and the others led their troops out of Xuzhou. As they neared Xiaopei, someone reported the news to Xuande. Xuande hastily consulted with his officers. Sun Qian said, “We should swiftly appeal to Cao Cao for aid.” Xuande said, “Who can go to Xudu to seek help?” A man below the steps came forward and said, “I am willing to go.” They looked and saw that he was a man from Xuande’s own commandery, surnamed Jian, given name Yong, style Xianhe, who was then serving as a retainer in Xuande’s staff. Xuande immediately wrote a letter and entrusted it to Jian Yong, ordering him to hasten by night and day to Xudu to request reinforcements. Meanwhile, he put the city’s defensive equipment in order. Xuande himself guarded the south gate, Sun Qian the north gate, Yun’chang the west gate, and Zhang Fei the east gate. Mi Zhu and his younger brother Mi Fang were ordered to guard headquarters. As it happened, Mi Zhu had a younger sister who had married Xuande as his second wife. Thus Xuande and the brothers were related by marriage, and for that reason he ordered them to guard headquarters and protect his wife and children.

p.src: When Gao Shun’s army arrived, Xuande called from the gate tower, “Fengxian and I bear each other no grudge. Why have you brought troops here?” Gao Shun replied, “You conspired with Cao Cao to harm my lord. Now the matter has been exposed—why do you not submit to bonds?” Having said this, he waved his army forward to attack the city. Xuande shut the gates and would not come out. The next day, Zhang Liao led troops in an attack on the west gate. From atop the wall, Yun’chang called to him, “Your bearing is far from common. Why have you cast yourself into the service of a villain?” Zhang Liao lowered his head and said nothing. Yun’chang perceived that the man possessed a loyal and righteous spirit, so he added no harsh words and did not ride out to fight him.

p.src: Zhang Liao withdrew his troops to the east gate, whereupon Zhang Fei rode out to meet him in battle. Someone quickly reported this to Lord Guan. Lord Guan hurried to the east gate and saw that Zhang Fei had only just emerged from the city while Zhang Liao’s army had already withdrawn. Zhang Fei wished to pursue, but Lord Guan urgently called him back into the city. Zhang Fei said, “He withdrew out of fear. Why should we not pursue him?” Lord Guan said, “That man’s martial skill is no less than yours or mine. My upright words moved him, and he felt considerable remorse; that alone is why he would not fight us.” Zhang Fei then understood. He merely ordered the soldiers to hold the gates firmly and no longer went out to fight.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jian Yong reached Xudu, met Cao Cao, and related the whole affair in detail. Cao Cao immediately assembled his advisers and said, “I wish to attack Lü Bu. I do not fear interference from Yuan Shao; I fear only that Liu Biao and Zhang Xiu may harry our rear.” Xun You said, “Those two have only lately been defeated and will not dare move rashly. Lü Bu is valiant and fierce. If he should further ally himself with Yuan Shu and range freely across the Huai and Si regions, it will soon become difficult to deal with him.” Guo Jia said, “We should now take advantage of the fact that his rebellion has only just begun and the people’s hearts have not yet attached themselves to him, and strike him with all speed.”

p.src: Cao Cao followed this counsel. He immediately ordered Xiahou Dun, together with Xiahou Yuan, Lü Qian, and Li Dian, to lead fifty thousand troops in the vanguard, while he himself commanded the main army and advanced behind them in successive divisions. Jian Yong accompanied the army. Scouts soon reported the news to Gao Shun. Gao Shun sent an urgent report to Lü Bu. Bu first ordered Hou Cheng, Hao Meng, and Cao Xing to take over two hundred horsemen to reinforce Gao Shun and meet Cao Cao’s army thirty li from Pei. He himself followed with the main force to support them.

p.src: Now Xiahou Dun led his army forward and came face-to-face with Gao Shun's forces. Leveling his spear, he rode out and challenged him to battle. Gao Shun rode out to meet him. Their horses crossed, and after they had fought forty or fifty bouts, Gao Shun could hold out no longer and fled from the field. Dun spurred his horse in pursuit, while Gao Shun fled around the battle lines. Dun would not relent and chased him around the lines. From within the ranks, Cao Xing saw what was happening. Secretly taking up his bow and nocking an arrow, he waited until his aim was sure and let fly. The arrow struck Xiahou Dun squarely in the left eye. Dun cried out and hastily pulled the arrow free with his hand, but to his horror, the eyeball came out with it. He shouted, “The essence of my father and the blood of my mother—I cannot cast it away!” He thrust it into his mouth and swallowed it, then leveled his spear once more, spurred his horse, and charged straight at Cao Xing. Before Cao Xing could defend himself, a single thrust pierced him through the face, and he fell dead beneath his horse. Every soldier on both sides who witnessed it was struck with horror.

p.src: Having slain Cao Xing, Xiahou Dun wheeled his horse around. Gao Shun pursued him from behind and signaled his whole army to charge. Cao Cao's forces suffered a crushing defeat. Xiahou Yuan protected his elder brother as they fled. Lü Qian and Li Dian led the defeated troops back to Jibei and made camp there. Victorious, Gao Shun led his army back to attack Xuande, just as Lü Bu's main force arrived. Lü Bu divided his forces into three columns with Zhang Liao and Gao Shun, and together they assailed the three camps of Xuande, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei. Indeed:
